question: Should OpenClaw add a model-facing parent-scoped send primitive for sub-agents, and if so should it be a dedicated `sessions_send_parent` tool or a `sessionKey: "parent"` resolver on `sessions_send`?
rationale: The change would let child agents wake or steer parent sessions mid-run, so automation cannot safely choose the API shape or isolation guarantees without maintainer intent.

options.title: Dedicated parent-send tool
options.body: Add `sessions_send_parent` that derives the target from trusted spawn metadata and rejects missing parent, sibling, ancestor, cross-agent, and chained forwarding cases.

options.title: Parent alias on sessions_send
options.body: Teach `sessions_send` to accept only the literal `sessionKey: "parent"` from sub-agents while preserving the existing denial for arbitrary session keys.

options.title: Keep announce/yield only
options.body: Do not add a mid-run child-to-parent send path and keep orchestration on completion handoff plus `sessions_yield`.

recommendation.title: Dedicated parent-send tool
recommendation.body: Add `sessions_send_parent` that derives the target from trusted spawn metadata and rejects missing parent, sibling, ancestor, cross-agent, and chained forwarding cases.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior issue review and recent session/sub-agent/docs history make steipete the best available routing candidate for the security/product decision.
